title: Doubloon SDK fails to load music stems

posts.cooked:
Hey everyone, I just wanted to bring up a pretty frustrating issue I’ve been running into with the Doubloon SDK. When I try to load music stems into either game-1 or game-2, the SDK just refuses to recognize or play them. It’s like the files are there, but the engine can’t access the different audio layers separately, which really limits how much you can customize the soundtrack in mods or custom content.

I saw a few mentions in other threads about this being an ongoing problem, and apparently it’s marked as “won’t-fix” by the devs, which is a bummer. For anyone hoping to do more advanced audio work, it means we’re stuck without proper stem support, and that feels like a missed opportunity for expanding the audio design possibilities. Has anyone found any workarounds or third-party tools that might help bypass this limitation? Would love to hear if you’ve cracked it somehow.

Yeah, I ran into the same issue when trying to mod the soundtrack for my project. The Doubloon SDK just refuses to load the separate music stems correctly, which makes layering and mixing the tracks almost impossible. It’s frustrating because the rest of the tools work fine, and you’d think something as core as that would be bulletproof.

From what I’ve gathered in other threads, this seems to be a longstanding bug that the devs have flagged as “won’t fix,” which is a real bummer. It’s like they’ve moved on to other priorities and left this problem hanging. If anyone has found any kind of workaround—like manually splitting audio files outside the SDK or alternative import tricks—it would be great to hear about it. Otherwise, we’re stuck with full mixes only, which really limits what we can do creatively.

posts.cooked:
I ran into the same issue while trying to get music stems working in Game-1 using the Doubloon SDK. It seems like the stem loading function just doesn’t trigger properly, and sometimes the SDK throws an error that doesn’t really explain what went wrong. From what I’ve gathered, this might be tied to some compatibility problems with how the SDK handles file paths, especially if your project folders have special characters or spaces.

Unfortunately, I haven’t seen any signs of this getting patched anytime soon — the devs marked it as “won’t-fix,” which is pretty disappointing. The workaround I’ve found is to bundle the stems manually as one track and then use audio cues to simulate stem switching in-game, but it’s definitely a hassle and not as clean as letting the SDK do it natively.

If anyone has found a more reliable hack or tool that can split or load stems externally without causing crashes, I’m all ears. Until then, I guess we just have to avoid relying on Doubloon for multi-track music in these games.

posts.cooked:
I’ve been poking around with the Doubloon SDK too, and yeah, the music stem loading issue is definitely a pain. It seems like the SDK just doesn’t recognize the newer stem format introduced in the latest patches of game-1 and game-2. I’ve tried re-exporting my stems in different formats, but no luck so far. Honestly, it feels like the SDK hasn’t kept pace with the way the sound team updated their audio files.

Someone mentioned “won’t-fix” in the bug tracker, which makes me worried this might never get officially addressed. If that’s the case, modders and musicians could be stuck with limited options unless they reverse-engineer their own workaround. For now, the only semi-solution I found is converting stems into a more basic multi-track audio file before importing, but it strips some of the flexibility we’d want for dynamic music layering.

I’m curious if anyone has come up with a clever hack or third-party tool that bridges this gap? Sharing any scripts or utilities would be a huge help, especially before the community splits over which platform supports better audio customization. Fingers crossed the devs revisit this someday, but until then, we might have to improvise!

Yeah, I ran into this exact issue when trying to mod some tracks in Game-1 using the Doubloon SDK. The stems just don’t want to load properly, which makes it impossible to tweak individual layers like drums or vocals. I was hoping for a quick fix or at least a workaround, but it seems like the SDK itself is pretty limited in handling these files.

From what I gathered, this is kind of a known problem that the developers aren’t planning to address anytime soon, especially since they marked it as “won’t-fix.” It might be tied to how the SDK was initially designed—maybe they never intended for full stem support outside of very specific use cases. Honestly, it’s a bummer because it really restricts what we can do with the music in both Game-1 and Game-2.

Has anyone found any alternative tools or methods for working around this? I was thinking maybe extracting the stems externally and then importing them manually, but that sounds kind of tedious. If anyone has tips or tricks, I’m all ears. Otherwise, looks like we’re stuck waiting for some miracle patch that probably won’t come.

I’ve been poking around the Doubloon SDK for a while now, and yeah, the music stems fail to load consistently—especially when switching between game-1 and game-2 projects. It seems like the SDK doesn’t properly handle the stem metadata or maybe it’s an incompatibility issue with how those files are packaged. I tried re-importing the stems in different formats, but no luck so far.

Honestly, given the “won’t-fix” status, I’m starting to think the best workaround is to handle your music stems externally and just sync everything manually in your game code. Not ideal, but at least it keeps your audio workflow moving. If anyone figures out a hack or a community tool to patch this, please share—this bug is a real headache for anyone trying to do layered audio in these projects.

Yeah, I’ve been running into the same issue with the Doubloon SDK not loading music stems properly. It looks like the system just glosses over the individual tracks, so you end up with this weird, blended audio that kills any chance of remixing or dynamic layering. I dug through some of the config files, but there’s no obvious workaround or setting to fix this on our end.

From what I’ve heard in other threads and dev posts, it seems like this might be an intentional limitation or something they’ve deprioritized fixing. It’s frustrating because the whole point of the SDK was to give creators more granular control over the sound design. Without the stems, a lot of that creative flexibility just evaporates. Hopefully, they reconsider and patch this in the near future, but for now, I guess we’re stuck with what we’ve got.

In the meantime, some folks have suggested manually extracting audio tracks outside the SDK before importing assets, but that’s a pretty tedious workaround. If anyone else has found a slicker fix or a better approach, I’d love to hear it!

posts.cooked:
Yeah, I’ve run into the same issue with the Doubloon SDK where the music stems just refuse to load properly. It seems like every time I try to swap out tracks or layer different parts for game-1, the stems either don’t appear or cause the whole sound system to glitch out. From what I can tell, it’s not specific to just one game but happens across both game-1 and game-2, which makes me think it’s something fundamental in how the SDK handles audio files.

I’ve seen some people suggest workarounds involving converting stems into separate full tracks and then manually syncing them in the editor, but that obviously defeats the purpose of having multi-layered stems. The tag “won’t-fix” kind of bums me out, but it also makes sense if the SDK creators are focusing on other features instead of polishing this part. Honestly, for now, it feels like we either have to stick with flat music tracks or get creative with external tools to approximate the layering effect.

Hopefully, if the devs ever revisit this, they’ll open up better support for stem loading—it would make a huge difference for dynamic music in our projects. Until then, I’m just trying to keep things simple while still making my soundscapes feel lively. Anyone else found a neat hack around this, or are we all just waiting for a miracle patch?
